extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED and USPTO administrative staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for imposing an interim suspension of a registered practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, and related filing, notice, and account-dissociation requirements during disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for interim suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension may be ordered when there is evidence that the respondent committed a serious crime (e.g., a felony offense) and, in light of the respondent's failure to file a response, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director may request interim suspension predicated on evidence of a serious crime; if the Notice and Order cannot be delivered it may be published in the Official Gazette. The Order found interim suspension appropriate where Respondent failed to file a response and certified statements of conviction showed felony convictions (e.g., attempted sexual assault with force, aggravated battery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleged violations of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804 (disciplinary grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary complaints may allege violations of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b), 11.804(c), or alternatively 11.804(i) based on criminal convictions or other conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint in this matter was predicated upon Respondent's guilty plea and conviction; certified statements of conviction/disposition were attached to support the disciplinary charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to a hearing officer for formal disciplinary proceeding (37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: When interim suspension is entered, the Complaint shall be referred to a hearing officer for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order expressly refers the Complaint to a hearing officer in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5). A copy of the Complaint is attached and a hearing officer will adjudicate the formal disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may be granted limited recognition to practice before the Office commencing on the date of the Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date the Order is signed, solely for the purpose of facilitating compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is temporary (30 days) and narrowly circumscribed to allow the respondent to comply with obligations under § 11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and method for filing written answer to the Complaint (37 C.F.R. § 11.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's written answer to the Complaint must be filed with the hearing officer within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.36.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists specific filing addresses for mail and hand-delivery to the HUD Office of Hearings and Appeals (with two physical addresses) and requires filing a PDF version via email to OHA_filings@hud.gov. A copy of the answer must also be served on the OED Director by mail to a specified counsel address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice procedures (certified mail, publication if undeliverable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order should be mailed by certified mail to the respondent; if the Notice and Order cannot be delivered to the respondent, it shall be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order in this matter was mailed by certified mail (receipt numbers provided) and, when not deliverable, was published in the Official Gazette on specified dates. Publication may substitute for personal delivery when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of Official Gazette Notice of Interim Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette stating the respondent's name, registration number, that the respondent has been suspended on an interim basis, the predicate convictions and counts, and the statutory provisions under which the action is taken, and where disciplinary decisions are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides template text including registration number, summary of convictions (e.g., counts and factual summary), citation to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25 and 11.59, and a link to the OED FOIA Reading Room for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to government entities and state bar authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the Final Order to (i) appropriate employees of the USPTO; (ii) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and (iii) appropriate authorities of any state where the respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires direct notice to those categories of entities to ensure relevant authorities and stakeholders are informed of the disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifically directs Respondent to comply with § 11.58 (which governs obligations on suspension/disbarment such as client notifications and handling of files).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of respondent from Customer Numbers and electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s); Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or be added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision removes and forbids access to USPTO electronic systems tied to Customer Numbers during suspension and until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of review on suspension (no automatic stay)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks review of the suspension, any review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing for review does not stay the interim suspension; the suspension remains in effect during review unless a specific stay is granted by the relevant authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of service must state that the Final Order was sent to parties in the manner indicated, including mailing by first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to addresses provided under 37 C.F.R. § 11.1(a) and other addresses where OED reasonably believes respondent receives mail, and email to OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes an executed Certificate of Service showing certified mail to the respondent's listed addresses and an e-mail to OED Director counsel, demonstrating compliance with service obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral and attachment of Complaint to Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint alleging violations (and any certified statements of conviction) shall be attached to the Final Order and referred for further proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attaching the Complaint and supporting documents (e.g., certified convictions) provides the factual basis for referral and formal disciplinary adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of relief — other necessary relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order may include 'such other and further relief as the nature of this cause shall require.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This language reserves the ability to order additional remedial measures as appropriate to the particular circumstances of the disciplinary matter.
